name: openssl
notes: Added 2026-10-10 for Web Tranche 3B milestone B2: WebKit's curl backend (OpenSSLHelper, CurlSSLVerifier, CertificateInfoCurl) and WebCrypto (crypto/openssl) use the OpenSSL API; Source/cmake/OptionsWin.cmake and OptionsPlayStation.cmake find_package(OpenSSL REQUIRED).

3.5 is the current long-term-support series (3.0 and 3.5 are the LTS lines); 3.6 and 4.0 are non-LTS or remove interfaces WebKit 2.54 was written against. The tarball's SHA-256 matches the one the OpenSSL project publishes beside it.

build.configure_script ./Configure with the target linux-@CRT_ARCH@ (tools/crt-port-build.py substitutes the CRT architecture). no-asm keeps the build portable across the CRT hosts and avoids the perl-generated assembler; it is a performance item, not a correctness one.

CFLAGS -D__ANDROID__=1: OpenSSL treats `__linux && !__ANDROID__` as the glibc-specific branch (SysV shared memory in rand_unix.c, ucontext-based async, /dev/random select), none of which a Bionic-compatible libc provides (Bionic has no <sys/shm.h>); the Android branch is the one that matches the CRT surface. Scoped to this port's own compile; it is not installed in any header.

make_targets build_libs / install_targets install_dev install_runtime_libs: the libraries and headers only. The `openssl` command-line tool and its apps (speed, s_time) are not a web-stage need and use SysV shm, fd_set and getservbyname surface the CRT libc does not carry.

macOS shared tests run with CRT_CXX_RUNTIME_LINKAGE=shared (test-level env): the executable links libc.dylib, the libc every dylib of the port loads, instead of a second static libc.a (Mach-O two-level namespace: two malloc/pthread registries in one process).
